title: Towards Improved Sentence Representations using Token Graphs
claim: Our lightweight pooling on a frozen model matches or beats pooling baselines that use full fine-tuning or LoRA, with orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters.
layout: 3 side-by-side scatter plots sharing a top legend; log-scale x-axis of trainable parameters, performance on y-axis; ours at top-left of each
description: A single row of three scatter plots, one each for GLUE CoLA (single-sentence, MCC), RTE (sentence-pair, accuracy) and STSB (similarity, Spearman). A shared legend across the top maps colors to pooling methods: red [EOS], green Mean, yellow Max, gray AdaPool, and blue GLOT (Ours). Marker shapes show the adaptation regime: square for full fine-tuning, triangle for LoRA, circle for frozen LLM. The x-axis is trainable parameters on a log scale from 10^6 to 10^10, and the y-axis is task performance. In every panel the large blue GLOT circle sits alone at the top left, at about 10^7 parameters and the highest score. The baseline triangles (around 2x10^8 parameters) and squares (around 7x10^9) sit lower and further right. The eye goes first to the isolated blue dot.
caption: Fine-tuning large language models for sentence embeddings is computationally expensive. Our pooling method, GLOT, constructs a latent token-similarity graph from the outputs of a frozen model. It then refines token representations with a graph neural network before aggregation. This technique enables decoder-only models (like Mistral-7B), typically optimized for next-token prediction, to produce powerful sentence-level representations without requiring any fine-tuning.
abstract: Obtaining a single-vector representation from a Large Language Model's (LLM) token-level outputs is a critical step for nearly all sentence-level tasks. However, standard pooling methods like mean or max aggregation treat tokens as an independent set, discarding the rich relational structure captured by the model's self-attention layers and making them susceptible to signal dilution. To address this, we introduce GLOT, a lightweight, structure-aware pooling module that reframes pooling as relational learning followed by aggregation. Operating on the outputs of a frozen LLM, GLOT first constructs a latent token-similarity graph, then refines token representations with a graph neural network, and finally aggregates them using a readout layer. Experimentally, our approach is remarkably robust and efficient: on a diagnostic stress test where 90% of tokens are random distractors, GLOT maintains over 97% accuracy while baseline methods collapse. Furthermore, it is competitive with state-of-the-art techniques on benchmarks like GLUE and MTEB with 20x fewer trainable parameters and speeds up the training time by over 100x compared with parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods. Supported by a theoretical analysis of its expressive power, our work shows that learning over token graphs is a powerful paradigm for the efficient adaptation of frozen LLMs. Our code is published at https://github.com/ipsitmantri/GLOT.
